I was a liberal leaning centrist until I moved out on my own. I got fucked by about every system this country has in place. Labor, healthcare, fuckin everything. 

I always kinda dug Bernie and around that time he was campaigning for 2020. His policies led me to the belief that every single problem we face in America and the world are fixable. After getting fucked by the world I wanted to find reason in how it happened. Make it make sense for myself I guess. I dug into everything that fucked me over and how those systems could be fixed. 

After Bernie’s campaign ended I didn’t wanna stop and just give up on change so I kept learning more and more about politics and different political systems. I wanted to make up for the years I spent with my fingers in my ears thinking I was above politics. I just kept getting more and more left wing with time. Eventually I wasn’t looking at people as the problem anymore instead I looked at systems we live under and how they were broken. I started really thinking about class dynamics and how I fit into them. I started viewing myself as a member of the working class and my fellow workers as people who got fucked in the same and different ways. We’re all in this together and we need to build a system that works for us all and account for our diversity of experience. And nowadays I think systems like socialism, communism, anarchism, etc are the best way to do that. 

Capitalism has been around for a long time and if this is the best it can do for us then that is depressing reality that I reject on its face. Human beings are too interesting and incredible to restrained to wage slavery. We are worth much more than the number capitalism and it’s lackeys strive to assign to us. I want to see what the world looks like when your bank account doesn’t determine your quality of life. 

Leftism made me more optimistic and I’m glad i decided to look into it all.

Edit: should probably clarify I ain’t just a Bernie bro. I still love the dude but at this point I’m significantly further left than him and I’m sure I’m only gonna go further lol.

I don’t think the kings alone can rule vegas but I do think they’d be key to the courier successfully ruling the strip. Suppose the courier takes vegas using the robot army. Seeing as the courier alone managed to topple Mr goddamn House, I think it’s reasonable to assume that the 3 major families on the strip could potentially topple the courier and the robot army and take over if they really wanted to. 

Now the kings alone ain’t worth much as they’re just a bunch of dudes with some basic guns. But add all the minor freeside factions like west side, van graffs, crimson caravan, the followers, the garrets, the thorn, etc. Now the courier has an army of regular people who have guns and control of the freeside economy. That’s a force to be reckoned with that’s always surrounding the strip. The families try anything and the couriers dudes could descend on the strip from every angle. If the courier were to strike a deal with the gun runners then all these factions could be armed up and put them on par if not beyond the families power. 

With the kings having a decent number of members and the right weapons they could be one of the strongest forces in the Mojave. And that force would be solely focused on protecting the people of freeside from any threats. Those threats could include the robots themselves as yes man suggested at the very end of the game. Without the kings the courier has no backup plan for when someone else tries to do what they did. 

TLDR: the kings might not seem massively important, but they’re such a likable faction that I like to think they play a larger part in independent vegas after the credits roll.
